My wife and I lost our ish in disbelief so bad, lbvs. I'm thinking, "That's probably Zoey Starks. There's no way WWE would have another company's champion out there. But I'll be Buddha, Zeus, Odin, Shango, and two other gods-DAMNED if Zoey doesn't look like Jordynn. Same attire and all.".😂😂😂Then when it set in...lol. all I can say is although AEW is failing terribly right now, as a fan of many of the men and women on that roster. And they and AEW changed the game and lead it into something beautiful. Before they started opening the "forbidden doors", THIS was incredibly unlikely to take place. Even during the pandemic when they were beating WWE in the ratings, you could tell how much WWE was watching and learning from AEW. Changing the empty and silent staging, ring, and set up at the Performance Center with no crowds. To having other wrestlers full in for the sound effect of a crowd, after AEW did it. We had Jericho stab Moxley's eye out, then Moxley stabbing Ortiz (if I remember correctly) in his eye for revenge. Then I turn to watch WWE and Seth is taking it a step further, disgusting, wincing way. Forcing Rey's eye on the corner of the ring steps. You got Kenny Omega sing his belt collector run and becoming the longest reigning champion, then-fast forward and Reign returns and becomes WWE's version of what Kenny was to AEW, Impact, Triple A, etc. Hell, those who were on the roster during the pandemic got paid more and signed contracts to stay longer so they wouldn't leave and go to AEW and reinvent themselves. Although that was great wrestling and entertainment going on in a horrible time in the recent history of the WORLD. Instead of disrespecting or ragging or mocking other companies. I'd much rather see them come together and work better. It's helped them both. CM Punk leaves AEW-returns to the WWE. Edge leaves the WWE and shows up in AEW...AND WITH HIS ICONIC ENTRANCE SONG AND PYRO?!?! Wrestling is so much more awesome, entertaining, and pleasantly shocking when that damn blasted "forbidden door" is open, instead of closed.

text: I'm not black. I'm SE Asian British with a Native British girlfriend at the time that stayed in Harlem while backpacking the US and Canada. We stayed in a room just by the corner of Malcolm X and MLK back in 2K2. I used to get my ciggy in the corner shop that always had a crowd of men in front. There was also always a boy sat on the steps across our building looking up and down the road. First day I got stared at and the men were slow to part for me to get to the door. Following day, same thing. On the way out though I decided to have a smoke outside and said hello to the people. Soon as they heard my accent, all I heard was 'daaaaamn!'. At dusk, we'd be sat on the steps because the room was boiling. We got people stopping by to have a chat. Checked if we were ok, what we've seen, recommended places to go to and not to go to in Harlem. We stood out on that block. After a certain time, there was no other people but black people.  They were friendly but in a gruff and direct way. On our last day, the guys on the corner helped us with our luggage and called us a cab that wasn't yellow and was cheaper (so we found out). One of the guys then told the driver: 'Hey Akhmed, $5 up the block. If I hear you charged them more, you'll get shot next time you on my block, you hear?!'. text:
I worked at a larger matchmaking company and we had to ask people their racial dating preferences because it had become enough of a problem when clients complained that their matches were chosen on a race blind basis. 
Basically, enough people didn’t want to date certain races that it became a problem for the company’s bottom line (my anecdotal observations of people’s dating preferences lines up pretty well with Dataclysm, a book written by a co-founder of OKCupid).

This included a preference for black Brits or Europeans *over* black Americans (being an African American was often a deal breaker when people were really thinking about dating for marriage). 
In a lot of cases, this was also coming from black Brits and Europeans.

text:
Messi as a substitute is honestly a cheat code and has been his whole career. A fresh Messi about to enter a game where everyone has already depleted 50-60% of their energy levels must be one of the most disheartening things for any opposing teams to have to face. I have watched so many games where Messi has come on as a sub and totally dominated. I actually used to wonder if a manager might use it as an actual tactic knowing if the team could stay in the match for 60 mins they are virtually guaranteed the points when Messi comes on. But of course it is very hard to leave the GOAT out of the starting line up, ironically I think if Messi played the last 30 mins of every game in his career, he might have ended up with hundreds more goals and assists than he does now, how crazy is that. 

No other player comes on as a sub and dominates like he has over the years, it is because he is that talented and skilful. For other players it is like running on a treadmill for an hour and then going off to defend Messi, they know it is impossible and they literally fear it, there are no other players who will instil fear in this way.

text: People complaining about the small capacities of the stadiums. There's a reason for this, and it's not because soccer isn't all that popular in the US. If you keep the capacities low, that causes demand. Higher demand = higher prices. They don't care about how many fans they can get into a stadium, but how much money they can make from over-inflating the price per seat.  Now, if soccer does start to become more popular and the fan base grows to something like the NFL (which it wont), they will be forced to expand, but until then, they will happily price gouge us. Notice that ticket prices in stadiums with massive amounts of seating (shared stadiums) don't charge as much as soccer specific stadiums.

The immense screaming made it impossible to hear the music, creating an iconic moment of Beatlemania.
Tickets ranged from $4.50 to $5.75 and sold out in less than three weeks.

text: My brother and I were 2 of the 55,000 who were fortunate enough to attend this concert! We had to send away for tickets and it was on a first come first served basis. The seats we wound up getting were at the mezzanine level right behind home plate and the Beatles performed on a platform located on second base facing our direction. Not even this concert footage could capture the absolute exhilarating insanity of being part of this wild crowd. From the moment the Beatles entered from the dugout and took the stage it was non-stop screaming and shouting with camera flash bulbs going off throughout the stadium. Fans passing out, crying and shouting out their names with several fans attempting to run onto the field! For the full 30 minute performance by the Beatles I recall all the hair on my 13 year-old body standing on end! The stadium speaker system wasn’t equipped to deliver quality sound as this was the first musical concert ever to be held in a stadium. While sound quality wasn’t the best we were still able to uncover what song the Beatles were playing despite the screams and shouts! It was a magical night that I found to be both thrilling and quite frightening dealing with “Beatlemania!”  It’s a memory that’s lasted a lifetime and it makes me happy to know that even the Beatles regarded this concert to be their most memorable one! BTW - we both returned to attended the Beatles at Shea in 1966 - mezzanine level at 3rd base. 😊

text: Atlanta is battling some bad luck and has some mentally broken players, it's obvious.  It's like every match someone hits a wonder goal against them and a GK makes an amazing save.  And it's a real problem with some players taking plays off.  I love Fafa's offense he brings but on that second goal by NE he took the entire play off, was late strolling into position and never even tried to mark, then Amador was a step slow and was beaten.  Saba is finished, he's a 31 year old winger who hasn't scored a goal in league play since 2024.  Latte Lath, sell him if you can or just eat his contract because they desperately need goals and you can't have a DP striker making $4M a year in wages who doesn't score goals.  He's broken and he may be permanently broken.  I couldn't believe they signed him for the amount they paid.  And I beg you, sign a good 6.  Ronny Deila had won 4 championships in 4 different leagues in Europe and North America, including MLS Cup, and had never failed until he failed in Atlanta.  Now it looks like even Tata can't get these guys to play better.  It's almost impossible now to say the problem isn't these players.
